# Claims register

**Generated by `scripts/56_claims_register.py` — do not edit by hand.**

Every claim this project makes, in one place, with its current status.
Scattered across nineteen reports these distinctions blur, and the
blurring always runs one way: a withdrawn mechanism gets quoted as though
it still stood.

The register is checked, not written. Every claim marked ESTABLISHED must
cite a check in `31_verify_claims.py` that exists, every cited report must
exist, and any verifier check cited by nothing is reported as a coverage
gap — which asks whether the evidence base and the story have drifted
apart.

| status | meaning |
|---|---|
| **ESTABLISHED** | survived its challenges; backed by a recomputed check |
| **LIMITATION** | a measured property of the corpus or method, not a result |
| **WITHDRAWN** | asserted earlier, retracted on evidence; do not quote |
| **UNANSWERABLE** | this data cannot decide it — not the same as 'no' |
| **EXPLORATORY** | not preregistered; hypothesis-generating only |

## ESTABLISHED (13)

### C01

The reference decoder works: 54.6° held-out error against a measured 90.7° chance level on T11, 52.8° on T5.

- **Report:** [`PHASE3_REPORT.md`](../reports/PHASE3_REPORT.md)
- **Checks:** 3 — `Reference decoder, T11 held-out healthy error (deg)`; `Reference decoder, T11 measured chance (deg)`; `Reference decoder, T5 held-out healthy error (deg)`
- **Note:** Chance measured by shuffled pairing, not assumed to be 90°.

### C02

The monitor detects faults that counting spikes cannot see, on both participants: AUC 0.69–0.71 with a local baseline where a calibrate-once baseline sits at chance.

- **Report:** [`EWS_RESULTS.md`](../reports/EWS_RESULTS.md)
- **Checks:** 3 — `Early-warning AUC, T11 recent-normal`; `Early-warning AUC, T5 recent-normal`; `Early-warning AUC, T11 calibrate-once (should be chance)`
- **Note:** Replicated. The calibrate-once arm is the control and lands at 0.491.

### C03

No configuration is deployable at the specified false-alarm budget: 0 of 48 pass all five gates.

- **Report:** [`BENCHMARK_SUMMARY.md`](../reports/BENCHMARK_SUMMARY.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `Configurations passing all five gates`
- **Note:** The binding gate is silence, not detection.

### C04

A session contains roughly one independent measurement: lag-1 autocorrelation of the risk signal is 0.995 (T11) and 0.980 (T5).

- **Report:** [`AGGREGATION_LIMIT.md`](../reports/AGGREGATION_LIMIT.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `Lag-1 autocorrelation of risk, T11 healthy`; `Lag-1 autocorrelation of risk, T5 healthy`
- **Note:** This single fact explains most of the negative results.

### C05

A task change is separated from a real fault by 15× on T11.

- **Report:** [`EWS_RESULTS.md`](../reports/EWS_RESULTS.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `Task change vs real fault separation, day 658`
- **Note:** The comparator gate does its job.

### C06

Commissioning is cheap: ~20 healthy windows (about two minutes) reaches the accuracy the entire healthy record reaches, on both participants.

- **Report:** [`CALIBRATION_CURVE.md`](../reports/CALIBRATION_CURVE.md)
- **Checks:** 6 — `calibration T11, 20 windows (scattered)`; `calibration T11, entire healthy record`; `calibration T5, 20 windows (scattered)`; `calibration T5, entire healthy record`; `calibration T5, 40 windows CONTIGUOUS`; `calibration T11, 20 windows CONTIGUOUS`
- **Note:** Contiguous draw confirms the count translates into real minutes.

### C07

A monitor's fit does not measurably go stale over 142 days.

- **Report:** [`STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md`](../reports/STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `staleness permutation p, T11 (naive said 0.003)`; `staleness permutation p, T5`
- **Note:** The naive test said p = 0.003; permuting day labels gives 0.128.

### C08

Monitor accuracy varies enormously by session — 0.32 to 0.97 on T11 — and only about a quarter of that is sampling noise.

- **Report:** [`STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md`](../reports/STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md)
- **Checks:** 4 — `day-to-day AUC spread, T11 (min)`; `day-to-day AUC spread, T11 (max)`; `I-squared across days, T11`; `share of day variance that is sampling, T11`
- **Note:** Invisible to every pooled analysis, because pooling averages it away.

### C09

Session accuracy is strongly associated with that session's absolute decoder error (ρ = −0.720, p = 0.0055), preregistered with the direction committed in advance.

- **Report:** [`DAY_PREDICTORS.md`](../reports/DAY_PREDICTORS.md)
- **Checks:** 4 — `P5 decoder error vs monitor AUC, T11 (rho)`; `P5 p-value, T11 (Bonferroni threshold 0.01)`; `P5 partial rho controlling window length, T11`; `P5 controlling for achieved damage, T11 (strengthens)`
- **Note:** Survived three challenges: early-warning window length, crossed/split shift, and the achievable-damage ceiling.

### C10

The bad-session pattern is shared by distribution-based detectors and absent from scalar ones — it belongs to a class of monitor, not to this implementation.

- **Report:** [`DAY_EFFECT_ACROSS_DETECTORS.md`](../reports/DAY_EFFECT_ACROSS_DETECTORS.md)
- **Checks:** 3 — `guard vs distribution_shift per-day AUC, T11`; `guard vs mean_activity per-day AUC, T11`; `distribution_shift vs decoder error, T11`
- **Note:** My prediction was that all four detectors would share it. They do not.

### C11

No label-free signal predicts whether the monitor will work that day, so abstention is an untested proposal rather than a capability.

- **Report:** [`ABSTENTION.md`](../reports/ABSTENTION.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `L4 vs monitor AUC, T11 (stage 2 null)`
- **Note:** Four candidates, two stages, nothing passes stage 2.

### C12

Mean output speed tracks decoder error on both participants and clears the threshold on both — with OPPOSITE signs (+0.681 vs −0.943).

- **Report:** [`ABSTENTION.md`](../reports/ABSTENTION.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `L4 vs decoder error, T11 (sign reverses)`; `L4 vs decoder error, T5 (opposite sign)`
- **Note:** Strongest cross-participant agreement in the project, and a contradiction: any rule tuned on one array runs backwards on the other.

### C13

Pooling episodes across sessions costs essentially nothing (0.003 AUC), refuting the hypothesis that pooling was diluting the signal.

- **Report:** [`STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md`](../reports/STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `cost of pooling episodes across days, T11`
- **Note:** Tested because it was attractive; reported because it was tested.

## LIMITATION (7)

### L01

Severity is only valid in aggregate: the three fault levels are correctly ordered in 57% of session × mode cells on T11 and 67% on T5, degrading with the session's baseline error on both arrays.

- **Report:** [`SEVERITY_LADDER_VALIDITY.md`](../reports/SEVERITY_LADDER_VALIDITY.md)
- **Checks:** 4 — `severity ladder monotone fraction, T11`; `severity ladder monotone fraction, T5`; `baseline vs ladder validity, T11 (rho)`; `baseline vs ladder validity, T5 (rho)`
- **Note:** The only relationship in this project that replicates significantly with the same sign on both participants.

### L02

Every AUC reported here understates performance by about 0.7–1.2%, because six 'pre-onset' windows per episode contain faulted data.

- **Report:** [`WINDOW_OVERLAP.md`](../reports/WINDOW_OVERLAP.md)
- **Checks:** 4 — `contaminated windows per episode, T11 (1500/250 = 6)`; `AUC understated by the overlap, T11`; `AUC understated by the overlap, T5`; `sign test across both arrays, p (one-sided)`
- **Note:** The bias is conservative, as was argued when found — now a number rather than an argument. No conclusion changes.

### L03

On sessions near chance an injected fault does almost no measurable damage, so their ground truth is nearly degenerate: 6 of 13 T11 sessions cannot be scored on unambiguous faults at all.

- **Report:** [`UNAMBIGUOUS_EPISODES.md`](../reports/UNAMBIGUOUS_EPISODES.md)
- **Checks:** 3 — `T11 days scoreable on unambiguous faults (of 13)`; `bad days retain fewer unambiguous faults, T11 (rho)`; `ceiling: baseline vs achieved fault damage, T11`
- **Note:** Day 783: 1 of 20 faults measurable. Day 672: none.

### L04

The profile covariance is singular below n = K + 1 windows, so the n = 10 calibration point is not a measurement.

- **Report:** [`CALIBRATION_CURVE.md`](../reports/CALIBRATION_CURVE.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `n=10 profile covariance is singular (min eigenvalue)`; `n=20 profile covariance is well posed (min eigenvalue)`
- **Note:** It is also the highest AUC on T11, and would have supported a false headline that more calibration data makes the monitor worse.

### L05

Inverse-variance weighting is biased for a bounded statistic: it inflated a pooled AUC from 0.675 to 0.836 by over-weighting the most extreme days.

- **Report:** [`STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md`](../reports/STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `inverse-variance weighting bias, T11 (rho)`
- **Note:** The field is named ..._BIASED_DO_NOT_QUOTE in the output.

### L06

The two participants disagree on why sessions differ: on T5 the spread tracks the fault mix each session drew, on T11 it does not.

- **Report:** [`STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md`](../reports/STALENESS_AND_DAY_VARIANCE.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `fault-mix confound, T5 (rho) — why T5 cannot corroborate`; `fault-mix confound, T11 (rho) — day effect stands`
- **Note:** So T5 cannot corroborate the T11 day effect.

### L07

A candidate feature can clear the bar on one participant and fail badly on the other (F3 spectral: 0.750 vs 0.556).

- **Report:** [`FEATURE_STUDY_RESULT.md`](../reports/FEATURE_STUDY_RESULT.md)
- **Checks:** 3 — `F3 spectral, T11 (cleared the bar here)`; `F3 spectral, T5 (failed badly here)`; `F0 control, T11 (current features, generic scorer)`
- **Note:** The both-participants rule in action; this is why it exists.

## WITHDRAWN (3)

### W01

WITHDRAWN: that the monitor fails because the decoder has lost its signal. Margin over a session's own chance level does NOT predict monitor accuracy (+0.264, p = 0.38).

- **Report:** [`WHAT_DECODER_ERROR_MEANS.md`](../reports/WHAT_DECODER_ERROR_MEANS.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `margin over own chance vs monitor AUC, T11`; `day 800 barely beats its own chance, P(better)`
- **Note:** Days 800 and 783 beat their own chance by near-identical margins with accuracies of 0.97 and 0.32.

### W02

WITHDRAWN: any claim about WHICH property of a session causes the accuracy swing. Trace noise predicts identically (−0.720) and correlates with decoder error at 0.813; the partials are identical in both directions (−0.333).

- **Report:** [`CEILING_CHALLENGE.md`](../reports/CEILING_CHALLENGE.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `trace noise vs monitor AUC, T11 (ties P5 exactly)`; `P5 controlling for trace noise, T11 (collapses)`
- **Note:** Identical partials both ways is collinearity, not mediation.

### W03

WITHDRAWN: that weaker faults on bad sessions explain the accuracy swing. Achieved damage barely relates to monitor accuracy (+0.181, p = 0.55).

- **Report:** [`CEILING_CHALLENGE.md`](../reports/CEILING_CHALLENGE.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `ceiling: damage vs monitor AUC, T11 (predicted +, got ~0)`
- **Note:** I predicted this confound would hold. It did not.

## UNANSWERABLE (1)

### U01

Whether the session effect is failed detection or degraded labels cannot be decided with this corpus: filtering to unambiguous faults leaves 7 sessions and ρ = −0.536, p = 0.215.

- **Report:** [`UNAMBIGUOUS_EPISODES.md`](../reports/UNAMBIGUOUS_EPISODES.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `P5 on unambiguous episodes only, T11 (underpowered)`; `spurious crossings vs monitor AUC, T11`
- **Note:** Not answered no — unanswerable. At n = 7, |ρ| must reach ~0.79 to clear p < 0.05, so the filtering removed the power along with the ambiguity.

## EXPLORATORY (3)

### E01

Sessions differ by a factor of fifty in how directionally varied the task was (0.013 to 0.679), which is why each session's own chance level ranges 47.7°–102.7° instead of sitting near 90°.

- **Report:** [`WHAT_DECODER_ERROR_MEANS.md`](../reports/WHAT_DECODER_ERROR_MEANS.md)
- **Checks:** 1 — `directional concentration vs monitor AUC, T11`
- **Note:** Not preregistered. Found while checking a recommendation I had already published, and it affects every absolute error number in the project.

### E02

Preregistered predictor P4 (within-day drift) came out with the wrong sign (+0.582 against a predicted negative) and P1 was null.

- **Report:** [`DAY_PREDICTORS.md`](../reports/DAY_PREDICTORS.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `P4 drift came out with the WRONG sign, T11`; `P1 healthy dispersion, T11 (null)`
- **Note:** Reported because the signs were committed in advance; nothing is claimed from either.

### E03

The decoder-guard operating point on T11 is 50.46, giving 3.41 false alarms per hour against a 0.1/h budget.

- **Report:** [`BENCHMARK_T11_local.md`](../reports/BENCHMARK_T11_local.md)
- **Checks:** 2 — `decoder-guard operating point, T11 recent-normal`; `decoder-guard false alarms per hour, T11`
- **Note:** Quoted in the demo; the budget is missed by 34×.
